tips.comment: Third on debut at Beverley in April and then the week before last won a maiden race at Chelmsford on the all weather. Trained by Charlie Johnston who has a top yard, I do think this is a chance for Cayman Dancer to win again and I think this Novice Stakes sees him win at an odds on price.

Londoner heads to Lingfield today after a narrow win at Newcastle over 1m2f just nine days ago. He carries a 5lb penalty for that success but remains on a competitive mark of 83 and could follow up if he maintains his current form.

Been in decent form recently and has been beaten less than 2 lengths in each of his last four starts. His latest effort, over this particular course and distance, saw him finish a close 3rd from the same mark he races off here. Was doing good work late on and with his yard still in good form, ought to go close.

Sugarloaf Lenny looks a little underrated here. It's as simple as that. There's not a lot to choose, statistically, between most of these so with the cheekpieces on, and after a good run last time out, there looks to be a bit of value here

Written off after a 14th of 14 at Chester, but showed promise in his run prior to that. He is interestingly 4/5 in fields smaller than 7, whilst also being 5/5 a place (2 wins) in this class. He looks to be floating around a dangerous turf mark on the balance of his form, and with a genuine lack of pace in here, he could be one to make it at his own pace, which has served him well in the past. 5 efforts on turf leave plenty to be desired, resulting in a record of 67500, so clearly he needs a career best on turf, which is why he’s the outsider ultimately, and that certainly tempers enthusiasm.
Good debut for new stable and won fairly comfortably in the end. Expect to lead here. It may be tactical and be hard to beat.

Urban Sprawl heads to Lingfield today after a solid fourth in a big-field handicap at York just five days ago. He’s back at a track where he’s won before and should get a handy position from today's draw so has a decent shot at going close.

Yantarni has not shown any form in a while, but this has resulted in his handicap mark dropping. Yantarni has run twice at this Lingfield course and distance and has won both times. In fact, his last Lingfield win was when wearing cheekpieces and was from a handicap mark of 77. Today, Yantarni has returned to a handicap mark of 77 and is wearing cheekpieces for the first time since last July.

Under The Twilight was not far away for both runs since the break. Even with a duff start and running out of steam at an extended mile in a C3 last time out, she could be worth a shot now back in C4 and down in trip off an 81. That's 5 lbs below her last winning mark.

Connections have found a decent opportunity for this one, down in grade/class and reverting back to turf. Had been running well in better races than this on AW and then was upped in class on the turf at Ascot last time when disappointing. Down significantly in grade here and can go well.

Fantasmic lines up in the 15:10 Download The Racecourse App Raceday Ready Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Class 5) at Lingfield, a 1m1f1y contest on good to firm ground. Trained by Jack Jones, this 3-year-old bay filly by Time Test out of River Belle has shown promise in her two career starts, finishing third on both occasions. 
Her most recent effort was a commendable third-place finish at Goodwood, indicating she's progressing with each run. With Rossa Ryan booked to ride, a jockey known for his tactical acumen, Fantasmic is poised to make a strong bid for victory.

In A Hurry, a 3-year-old bay filly, made a satisfactory racecourse debut last season as a 2-year-old but was then off the course for 10 months. Came back in April and ran well to finish 2nd again. Looks likely to go one better here.
Second last time, going and distance no problem. Jockey claiming three pounds, will be in the mix of things at the business end of the race. Nap each way at 5/1.

The Jonathan Portman-trained Hello Luna put in a much better performance last time out when beaten 1 1/4 lengths, finishing 4th of 10 over 5f at Windsor. The 3-year-old Hello Youmzain filly showed she has early speed and a liking for the quicker underfoot conditions. This is just her second start in a handicap and she has dropped a pound to 63. In my opinion, she should be winning one of these Class 5 handicaps in the near future.

Couldn’t turn it round quickly under a penalty, but is a few lbs better off here with a fairly plum draw in two in a race that lacks a front runner. If she can get a clean break from stall 2 she could dictate proceedings from a kinder racing weight up in class. With Leavy’s claim she’s back down to her winning mark, and seemed to win with enough authority to give her a chance here if getting the breaks.

Possibly in need of the run at Windsor earlier this month following an absence of 78 days. David Probert back on board looks a positive sign having ridden this filly to her sole career win over Brighton's extended 5 furlongs in September 2024. The first time cheekpieces could have a positive effect too.

Her stats make for grim reading with just one win from a total of 11 runs, but now running off the lowest career mark. I think she can build on her last time out effort here and will look to improve for the new yard.
Watkins was a good second to winner She Went Whoosh in April and joins her again off the same mark. Worth an EW chance.

This looks like a poor race, and Honour Your Dreams must have a great chance of following up on its last win. Ran at Windsor on May 12th, and the 5lb penalty looks fair in the context of this race. With only 4 runners in the field, the draw should not count so much, so all the horses have a fair chance.

Mart lines up at Lingfield today after a sixth-place finish at Leicester last month. He’s back at a track where he’s had success before, including a win over this trip and could be competitive if he finds his best form. ￼

Count Otto is 10 years old now, and that alone will put a lot of punters backing him. He has had a warm-up run after a massive 439-day break. Connections must have faith to not retire him, and I am not convinced any of this field are any better.

Toby Tops has been in cracking form, winning three of his last four, including a solid effort at Ascot over nearly two miles. He’s up 7lb but still looks well-treated off 69, and has a strong chance of keeping the run going.

Weddell Sea is the outsider in this 3-runner race where all 3 have won twice or more in their last few runs. I think the handicapper has the other 2 just a little high, leaving Weddell Sea a good shout at these odds.

Man Of La Mancha was unplaced in his first two starts but improved on his final start in a novice at Kempton in March when 3rd of 12. Switched to handicaps at Windsor last week, he showed himself to be better than his mark with a 2.25 lengths win. He has a 7 lbs penalty, but useful apprentice Jack Dace claims that back. He looks to have a great chance of following up.

Still not won on six starts but has been steadily improving and has placed on his last four starts most recently finishing a close third (by a neck) over today's trip at Doncaster four weeks ago. Yard in good form recently. Should be involved at the finish.

War Howl is a 3-year-old gelding trained by Michael Appleby. He is 0-6 wins but made an encouraging start on stable debut after a lengthy absence of a 190-day break, finishing 3/9 at Newcastle. He was beaten 3.25 lengths behind Tuco Salamanca, who was winning three races in a row. War Howl represents a stable that has plundered handicaps at Nottingham, picking up 77 handicaps since 2012. So the price shouldn't deter you from having a small wager at 16-1 in today's contest. Now stepped up in trip, with the dam winning over 8.5f, which could bring about some improvement. He is related to three other winners who recorded career-high RPR of 88-92-114. With William Buick on board, further progress off a lowly mark of 73 is very possible.

DARN HOT MYSTERY could be of interest for a yard who have enjoyed a hot recent spell and who could continue throughout this season. A stoutly bred three year old filly who may be fit enough to do herself justice and fresh from what appear a fair opening mark she could show up well.

Despite running green and jockey Lewis Edmunds not having his finest hour in the saddle Herculeus still managed to finish 2nd lto in a cl5 maiden at Windsor 22 days ago. This is his first run in a handicap and his mark of 73 seems fair. Trainers William Muir & Chris Grassick won this race last year with Liveandletlive and today on a kinder track I think we will see a better performance from both horse and jockey.

Everyoneknowsadave has demonstrated potential on the all-weather circuit, securing two wins from his last six starts, including a victory at Southwell over 1m13y in January 2025. His recent form includes a commendable fifth-place finish in a 1m handicap at Doncaster on May 3, 2025, where he was beaten just over three lengths on good to firm ground. With the going at Nottingham expected to be good to firm, conditions should suit Everyoneknowsadave well. His proven ability over the distance and recent form make him an appealing each-way proposition at likely generous odds. Tom Marquand takes the ride too, so he should be able to bring the pace out of this horse on the turn for home.

Was switched to the turf last time at Windsor and finished in midfield over a mile. Wasn’t given a particularly hard ride and moves into handicaps now from a low mark. Every chance of stepping up on that form here and worth a second look.
Not seen since last summer. Cost 650k as a yearling and has had just the 2 runs. In good hands and expected to go well here.

Zaramara represents the stable of Michael Appleby. In her only race, she didn't succeed, but she didn't fail. The increased distance should favor her. At 100/1 odds with this line-up, it looks like a straight betting incentive in each way.

Line through run last day as she was in season. But it's resulted in her making her handicap debut off 78, which will likely prove very lenient. Boughey money shouldn't be dismissed, and she has attracted heavy support on every start and obviously has shown all the right signs at home. She goes up in trip tomorrow, and while she could drift in the morning, I'd expect some further support before the off and looks to me like she will take a whole load of beating off this mark.

Manara lines up in the 16:02 Dine In Sherwoods Restaurant Fillies' Handicap (Class 4) at Nottingham, a 1m2f50y contest on good to firm ground. Trained by Kevin Philippart de Foy, this 3-year-old bay filly by Camelot carries a rating of 80 into this 15-runner field. 
Manara has shown consistent form, boasting a record of three wins and two runner-up finishes from her six career starts. Notably, she secured back-to-back victories at Wolverhampton in February and March 2025, demonstrating her versatility across different surfaces. Her latest outing saw her finish a close second at Brighton over 1m2f on April 29, 2025, where she was beaten by just over a length, indicating she's holding her form well.
Two poor runs this year, but won six times in 2024 and hoping to get back to that sort of form. Decent chance in this field.

CASTRO AURUM was a winner on her seasonal reappearance and looking feasibly treated for handicap company no real reason why she can't not build on that success. She has Ray Dawson aboard who is riding with plenty of confidence since a previous spell overseas and he has been among the recent winners.
Mrs. Twig managed four wins last term, including a reappearance win. The last winning run in C4 was off a 77 on GF in Sept and gets my vote now back with the fillies.
Ran a promising race on debut even though he wasn't fancied, starting at 33s. Cost 350k as a yearling and kept on gradually, racing for another day. Likely improver.
Showed significant improvement when runner-up at Chelmsford last time out in what was his first run over this distance. Can go one better here.

Trainer William Haggas has 3 runners in this race, all at decent-looking odds. It's a question of which one is going to improve best from the debut race, and the fact that this afternoon's jockey has picked this one to ride could be a clue.

The favorites for this race can't be said to have impressed with their previous results. What if we look at Tenable, who represents successful trainer William Haggas? This stable has a good track record of achieving debutant results. Tenable has an excellent pedigree with Frankel as his sire. There is a chance to surprise by winning a prize today.
Just a complete long shot, as it hasn't shown much of anything in two starts. But it's a weak field with some of the leaders not impressing on prior runs.

ANTIPHON carries top weight which is actually kind of a positive. Given how fast this 6-y-o has fell down the weights, this opposition ought to be manageable. True to point out the selection has only just about won his share and it has often been a long time between drinks. This 5f trip on good ground will suit though and definite claims if running somewhere near to form. Snow Berry and Masterclass both look credible win and place alternatives.

Banana finally got off the mark at the 48th attempt when scoring at Bath in early May. Then followed up with a strong 2nd at Bath over 5f 6 days ago, running like she was going to win again in good style. Banana is clearly thriving and holding her form very well. It is very hard to knock her attitude right now. She is consistent and running with renewed confidence after a long spell as a maiden. So with momentum on her side, Banana is a solid win shot again, especially at this modest level, and I very much respect her in her current efforts.

The 5yo has a hit and miss profile but is capable on his day and does like the fast ground. Back on quick ground last week when 11 of 15 but he was much better than the bare stats, beaten 3L. He messed up the break and lost plenty of ground and was at the rear. However, he did get into a challenging position a furlong out, the jockey never had to get serious, but he then got stuck in a pocket and the jockey had to stop riding in the last half furlong. He wasn’t beaten far last August on quick ground, while racing off a 15lb higher mark.

Stroxx has had a couple of wins this year, with the latest being in April off a 50 under Cian Horgan. The latest run at Catterick was a close second off a 51 and goes again with the same mark with Cian back on top with a 5 lbs claim and ground to suit.

Showing some improvement since the seasonal return to turf, with the better performance most recent, over 5f. Running a good race after an awkward start and running a bit green for the first 2f. Was also eased in the last half a furlong after no longer disputing for first. That race was won by Banana, who heads the market here. They both raced off 46 that day. Today, Banana races off 52, with Tilsworth Ony Ta still off 46. Jim Crowley on board again, who will understand the horse better now and, given a clean start, get him in a good position ready to pounce on the leaders at the end.

Can do much better than the LTO effort when only 14th of 15 at Catterick earlier this month. Hoping to be a lot more competitive now handicapping again and is 3 lbs lighter than the last winning mark.

Despite the slight drift in the market on the Jamie Snowden-trained Ghost Hunter, I think he has a very good chance of following up after only going up 2 lbs for his last win. The top-rated in the race is from the in-form James Owen yard but was a disappointing 5th of 5, beaten 25 lengths last time out, and has to give Ghost Hunter 8 lbs.

Jubilant is a hurdles winner and got off the mark in a Huntingdon handicap over 25f in February. The recent runs don’t leap off the page, but the bare form may not tell the full story here as it has shaped better than the results imply if you replay the races. Definitely has chasing potential and with Bowen onboard, it looks the type to do better over fences now, particularly given that he was runner-up in his only Irish point, which is a very encouraging start as a pointer to his chasing future. He may just come in today as there is more to come now sent chasing with Sean onboard.

Bowen is onboard again today and 2 pounds lower mark given. El Muchacho won on his chase debut for Harriet Dickin at Plumpton on Easter Monday 2023, but since then has struggled to replicate that form, including during a 4-run stint with Christian von der Recke. Now with the Olly Murphy yard, he showed some encouragement on stable debut when 3rd at Chepstow, suggesting there may still be a spark. But now he needs to build on that recent Chepstow effort. With the chase-winning experience and signs of revival for new connections, it makes him a worthy challenger, especially as the market is speaking in his favor today and he is the current favorite.

The model I run suggests Harel Du Marais is the value pick here and can win this race. The race simulation had Harel Du Marais in first, Jetronic in second, and El Muchacho in third. This result has largely been driven by Harel Du Marais having the second highest RPR for this 5-runner field. It does line up with a full stone less in weight to carry when compared to the current market leader, Duke of Luckley. Harel Du Marais is a previous course and distance winner and comes here after a good second only 12 days ago.
First run since November but did well over hurdles last year with a win and two places from just four runs. That win came here and also placed here on the flat.
Showed some ability on the flat previously and on her two hurdling starts. 3rd on her last start at Kempton 2m (good). This race is easier and first-time hood goes on. Should be in the mix.

Olly Murphy and Sean Bowen combo = a strong team with winning experience in nearly every race. No Tricks At All's pedigree is from No Risk At All, who is a top jumps sire. Half-sister to 4 winners, including Kazarov and Kap Sky, both of whom were successful over hurdles and fences in France. With a price tag of 125k as a 3-year-old, it indicates very strong expectations of him. Olly's bumper horses are in excellent form, which enhances confidence in me on its debut. Very well-bred, high price tag, and a yard in flying form over bumpers. Whats not to like? Seems to me that it could make a winning start here.

Top trainers Dan Skelton, Olly Murphy, and Nicky Henderson are represented here, all with promising-looking horses on breeding. But it could be worth taking a chance on Dan Horsford's representative, Beggar's Nap, who has a nice-looking pedigree as he is by Derby winner Wings of Eagles and from a very good family on the mare's side. Dan Horsford is not a well-known name yet, but he was assistant to Alan King and has made a promising start to his training career, including a first-time bumper second on Sunday.

I know, another Bowen-ridden horse I hear you say! However, this has been backed overnight and is literally falling to its lowest level in the weights since and is now the favorite today at the moment. Owned by the Bowen family and saddled by Sean himself puts confidence in this horse (they know what they are doing). Leading Force's previous successes included a win over a 21f chase at Sedgefield last year. His recent form is below par since that win, but he is now trained by James Owen, which could spark a revival in him. So what we have is recent form that is lacking, the handicap mark has dropped significantly, and the yard switch is an unknown potential, but he is well handicapped and very dangerous to dismiss.

2nd at Exeter back in March, and hasn't won since November back at Fakenham. Reverts back to hurdling and comes here on the back of a wind op to support performance further. The favourite 'Leading Force' races for the first time for a new yard but has something to find after losing by twenty-eight lengths or more in the last three races.

I do think that stable debutant Leading Force is a crazy price and he's worth taking on. LIZZIE REY travelled a lot kinder in first-time cheekpieces when scoring on her penultimate outing, where I thought she had something in hand. The subsequent quick turnaround can be forgiven and Richard Phillips' mare is effectively only 1lb higher than her triumph with Finn Lambert able to claim his 5lb.

Few miles on the clock for the 8-year-old. The better ground and 3m trip is ideal. A win and close 2nd last summer under similar conditions. Two runs this year after coming off a 7-month break. Not beaten far two weeks back, not given a hard time, and it could set him up nicely for this low-grade handicap.

The model I run suggests Fox's Socks can win this one. This race simulation result has largely been driven by Fox's Socks having a comparably high RPR compared to the field, but a very low OR. This leaves Fox's Socks carrying quite a bit less compared to the top weights in the market (1 stone 10 lbs!). Form looks decent too, ran a good 2nd 12 days ago. Three or four jockeys are claiming in this race and Aarson Anderson claims 5 lbs for Fox's Socks too, taking the weight differential to over 2 stone in some cases.

Moro Rock only had four runs last year but was placed in two of those. Although UR on the return last month on Chase debut, he now gets back hurdling and is second up after wind surgery, which is when I would expect improvement. He could be involved again EW.
Wins at big prices 80/1, 50/1, and was 2nd in this race last year at 40/1 after a long break. Comes back here again after a long break and must be in with a squeak e/w at 40/1.

Just four starts over hurdles for this 7yo, ex PTP runner. His best run was a close 3rd of 11 on his handicap debut when last seen. He’s been off the track for 7 months but going off his previous runs - waiting for better ground. He’s better off at the weights now. This is a low grade, weakening looking contest. The trainer has sent out 8 runners in the last two weeks - 5 winners for a huge 63% strike rate.

Down another 2 pounds and Bowen in the saddle to try and make him work today! Runaway Train definitely showed promise when 2nd on his handicap debut in a 15f here in November. In recent runs, he has failed to build on that since, posting 2 disappointing efforts. However, when you replay the races, you can see that he has potential and was willing, so a chance is taken today on him. So my mind says that the eye-catching handicap debut hinted at a better potential, and Bowen will make him work harder today, so he may just squeak in the win.
Only a few of these bring a recent run or any form into this. Ran nicely last time out on handicap debut and would be a surprise if not involved in the finish here.
Won three times back in 2023 but hasn't done a lot since then over hurdles or in chases. Worth a little look just in case able to get back to that level again at Southwell.

The model I run suggests Mac's Xpress can cause an upset here, and that the value play is each way on 41s. Mac's Xpress lines up with by far the highest RPR of this field, a good 10 points ahead of the next best rated 93. The official ranking suggests a much lower score and perhaps is the reason for the larger odds. Three places up for grabs in this 11-runner field, each way still offers value at that price. Back down in trip today to 2m 4f from much longer prior distances and looks to get back to good form by running off a reasonable mark.

Am Still Here just lost out in his first chase over course and distance by half a length after a protracted tussle with the eventual winner. Only raised by two pounds, he could get his first win. Sean Quinlan keeps the ride.

The model I run suggests the value bet here is each way on Royal Deeside. This horse lines up with the highest RPR of the field and is one of the younger ones here looking to progress. An official ranking, which is the second highest, leaves him carrying initially the second highest amount around this 2m 4f trip. He has shown glimpses of form before a break and looks to get back to near that form here today.
Well Educated's four course victories, including last year's renewal and a solid recent two-mile effort, make her a formidable challenger.

Willie Shake Hands won for the first time over course and distance 10 days ago. That had followed three placed finishes. He is 5 lbs higher here and 6 lbs worse off than re-opposing runner-up Dream Jet. He beat that one by 7 lengths, so should be able to confirm superiority and go in again.

The model I run suggests Dream Jet can win this one. Dream Jet lines up with the highest RPR of this 6-runner field but has an official ranking somewhere closer to the middle order. This leaves him carrying a decent weight and 6 lbs less than favorite Willie Shake Hands. Previous course and distance winner and looks to add another here. Ran only 10 days ago, so the main concern might be the quick turnaround.

Factor in the likelihood of an uncontested lead and conditions that mirror its preferred setup, and this entry stands out as a formidable contender. While the margin of its last victory may flatter slightly due to race dynamics, the core strength of the form is underlined by subsequent runs from rivals. With fitness assured and confidence soaring, expect another bold showing, potentially defying revised expectations to cement its status as a horse on the up.

A cheekpieces-wearing 8-year-old Irish horse, he has finished in the first three 7 times from 14 starts over hurdles. Most recently, he finished 3rd of 9 at Newcastle in March and 3rd of 8 at Carlisle in April, both over slightly further than today's distance but on similar good going. Joshua Thompson rode last time and partners again, claiming a useful 7 lbs.

First run this year and on its last winning mark and over the same course and distance as that win. A different jockey, but the jockey did come second on its run subsequent to the win. All in all, fitness notwithstanding, a possible for a place.

Cage Rattler looks interesting in this Hexham Handicap Hurdle. He won on the flat when trained in Ireland and was placed over hurdles at Newcastle in March. Unplaced in two runs since, he is now down 2 lbs, and with the drop back to 2 miles likely to suit, he looks a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

This is a weak looking race, so even though BLENDED STEALTH is still a maiden, he's been competitive on numerous occasions in the past. One such instance was over this distance in November, from a pound higher in the weights. Didn't offer much three days ago, so there's every chance connections pull him, but if they give him the once over and decide to go then maybe he'll get a look in at a big price.

Gemini Man did well under Danny McMenamin for two runs in February and March in C4 when second and a third. But he did not seem to get on with a change of rider for his C5 handicap hurdle debut and is worth another shot with Danny back on top. EW 4P
Came second here back in 2023 in good going. Total long shot but worth a play with four places and no real strong standouts.
Maxs Champ won well at Uttoxeter after a long break. Ridden by Benjamin Macey again, he should follow up at Hexham off top weight but only raised five pounds in the handicap.

The model I run suggests Tartan Cookie can win this one. This result has been driven by Tartan Cookie having a relatively high RPR compared to the field, but looks well treated off this official rating. Steps out carrying a mid-range weight and is a prior course and distance winner. Good first 17 days ago, so clearly comes here in good form.

MADEMEWHATIAM made an encouraging reappearance latest and that was his first start following wind-surgery. If it can be assumed that he will build on that effort then eased a further 2lb from his lowly hurdles mark he could be a well treated runner.
Looking past last month's run, as that was the first in nearly a year. Some strong contenders, but decent each way value here.

Halfway House Lad heads into today's race in excellent form, having won 2 of his last 3 by comfortable margins. Charlie Price rides again, carrying just 10st 4lb, only 9lb more than his previous winning weight. Trainer Maurice Barnes has a strong record at this track.

Kicksaftersix has won 3 times over fences and is on a hat trick after winning over course and distance last month and again 17 days ago. Both have been won comfortably, and a 5lb raise might not stop him from bringing up the hat trick.

The model I run suggests C'Est Quelqu'un can win this one. C'Est Quelqu'un lines up here with the highest RPR of the 9-runner field. Does carry the highest weight for that trouble, but there's not too much in it compared to some of the other lower-rated horses. Placed well 17 days ago, so comes here in decent form. Looks to get over the line first and build on top of that. Alan Doyle on board relieves a further 5 lbs, which makes it more competitive in the weights.

A midfield finish last time here and pulled up before that. Has run from OH at the course also but is a very poor 2/40 over fences. You get the feeling that a better run is on the cards and hopefully might grab a place here.

Lady Hamilton was travelling well enough in the race here won by Kickaftersix 17 days ago, a race in which most of today's field competed. It was just the 2nd chase start for her, and she was soon on her feet after her fall four out. If no worse for that, and she runs well again at these weights, she should be bang there at the finish with a clear round.

The Jamie Snowden-trained Doc McCoy won on his hurdling debut and was 4th under a penalty next time out but picked up an injury soon afterwards. Back from a break, he hasn't looked quite up to it over fences, and so he reverts back to hurdles, where he won well last time out. Up 2 lbs here, he should be able to go close again.
5/4

The model I run suggests Land Girls Luck can cause an upset here. This is only a 4-runner race, but Land Girls Luck steps out with a similar RPR to the current market favorite. Notably, it is marked lower in the official ranking, meaning they step out with supposedly the same potential but carrying less weight over the 2m 3f round trip. Freddie Mitchell relieves a further 5 lbs as a claiming jockey. Has shown glimpses of promise before, notably winning at Sedgefield over 2m 2f. Cheekpieces helped then, and Land Girls Luck goes out wearing them again today.
Best run came over good ground and could be well suited to conditions here. Reasonable opposition to the favorite in a small field.

The model I run suggests an upset from Dr. Lockdown. A 3-horse race due to early dropout, so no each-way availability here. This model result has been driven by Dr. Lockdown having a reasonably kind official ranking and a good 3rd place at Hexham 10 days ago. Is wheeled out again here in a quick turnaround, maybe looking to capture a decent score while in form. Long odds, this price of 14/1 means this kind of bet only needs to pay off once every 15 times (or 6.7% of the time) to break even. I'll take those chances.

Has an each-way chance if fit to go after another break. Ran her best race when last seen in November, making what looked like a potentially race-winning move to challenge before weakening out of it. Drops another pound here.

Decent 4yo filly, solid runs in three hurdle races in the second half of last year, two near misses. The 2m trip on good ground will suit her. Now making her handicap debut and there could be improvement after 6 months off the track.
Hasn't done badly since switching to hurdles, coming second (of three) and a decent fourth place last time out. Could push on here.

The model I run suggests Lady Buttercup can cause an upset here. This model result has largely been driven by Lady Buttercup having a relatively high RPR compared to the rest of the 7-runner field, but does go out with the lowest official ranking. This leaves Lady Buttercup carrying the lowest amount of weight on this 1m 7f trip. Lady Buttercup is a prior distance winner, one of only two on the card. Comes back after a long break of 109 days. Previously won a 2m NHF at Warwick in September and hasn't really kicked on since. But this mark looks a bit more workable. Charlie Maggs claims a further 5 lbs, so the total weight difference to the last run is the best part of a stone.

The model I run suggests High Court Judge can win this race, ahead of Noisy Jazz and Arcon. High Court Judge goes out for only the second time over hurdles, so is relatively unexposed. Would have picked up good experience from the first run and was a serial winner on the flats, winning 8 times and placing over 15 times in 32 races. Previous run in May was on good to soft, Huntingdon is officially good ground and might suit better around this 1m 7f maiden hurdle race. Ben Bromley on board relieves a further 5 lbs and takes the total weight being carried down towards the lower order.
Could be one of the stronger challengers to the heavy favorite. Did well in flat and on all weather and picked up a few places. Some of the others here seem genuine outsiders.

Class 4 maiden hurdle over 2 miles at Huntingdon. Six runners and only two of them have previous hurdles experience, one of whom is Velvet Vulcan who runs for Mike Murphy. Michael Keady (the pair formerly associate trainers) runs Venus Slipper who scored over ten furlongs on the AW earlier this year. Damsire is Dubawi. Four year old filly so gains a weight allowance off many of these. Each-way squeak.

It's amazing what a change of scenery does to a horse. To be fair, Shadows In The Sky has always been a decent type since watching him finish 2nd at Musselburgh on hurdling debut for former trainer Chris Grant and former owner David Armstrong. Now with James Owen, and with his stable is on fire, I don't see why he shouldn't follow up here with conditions in his favor.

The model I run suggests Prospect House can win this one. Prospect House lines up here with a comparable RPR to the rest of the runners, but a materially lower official ranking. Steps out carrying a massive 2 stone (!) less than the current market favourite Shadows In The Sky. Prospect House won 30 days ago at Market Rasen over a slightly shorter distance. William Maggs on board claims a further 5 lbs off Prospect House's back, taking the total weight difference to Shadows In The Sky to 2 stone and 5 lbs. This kind of weight differential and form difference over 2m 3f will surely be telling.
Runner-up over a furlong and a half shorter at Ascot under today's jockey last time out and worth another look over this longer trip off the same mark.

The model I run suggests Dear Ralphy should win this race. The race simulation result had Dear Ralphy in first, Lilyhan in second, and Kitesurfer in third. This result has largely been driven by Dear Ralphy having a comparable RPR to the rest of the runners, but a materially lower OR. This leaves him running off a lower mark than the rest and carrying less weight over this 3m 1f trip. Dear Ralphy goes out carrying over a stone less than Kitesurfer and 2 stone less than Lilyhan. This is significant over 3m 1f.
Made his racecourse debut over this C&D two weeks ago and shaped with promise amongst clear signs of greenness. Every chance of leaving that bare form behind and looks to hold solid claims.

Wasn’t beaten far over this c&d when making her debut, doing well to finish as close as she did after having anything but a clear passage during the race. Capable of building on that and can reward each way interest.
Shaped better than the result last time when the rider stuck to the inside rail, and he just couldn't get out. Looked to have plenty of horse under him, and he comes here off the same mark.

Back from a six month absence when finishing a close 3rd in a 7.5f handicap at Roscommon 9 days ago. Was travelling well when encountering traffic problems and under the circumstances did well to finish so close. Races off a lb higher mark today but looks sure to go close in this smaller field.
Improved on her first six starts to win over today's trip at Dundalk last month when returning from four months off. Yard in good form recently. Should be thereabouts

An open-looking basement sprint where Realtin Fantasy appeals at a big-looking 16/1. He is largely consistent but has dropped to a very good-looking mark and has landed a plum draw in stall 15 (high numbers vastly favored here).

LAKOTA LADY steps back down to the minimum trip ahead of her third handicap. She shaped with plenty of promise on her penultimate start and was looked after when meeting with trouble latest. She could be a mare approaching her peak now as a five year old.

Twotolose is a lightly raced gelding with limited experience but has shown glimmers of promise. The latest run was 15 of 20 at Navan over 5f 24 days ago. This was after a 6-month layoff and wearing a hood for the first time on its layoff first run, which it may have needed. Hood and tongue strap now fitted and an EW chance here. Might strip fitter for that first run reappearance and is still unexposed here. Definitely not dismissed, especially if showing more pace and sharper fitness.

Quite a lot to like about her racecourse debut at the Curragh last month when finishing well having been given plenty to do. Finished in midfield but ran better than that might suggest and it was a similar story at Gowran last time. This looks a tough race before handicaps become an option and probably playing for minor honours.

TSWALU has been placed in two races from two starts. Second over 1m 1f at Gowran Park on her latest outing earlier this month. Upped in trip to 1m 4f should suit and could well be able to go one better and win this race.

Royal Entry is still a maiden after 7 starts, but she has a great chance of getting off the mark here. She has been runner-up 3 times, including her last 2 starts. She was second over this 1m4f trip at Curragh in November. She moved to Paddy Twomey's yard in April and was second again on stable debut at Killarney last week over 8 furlongs. She should benefit from the return to 12 furlongs, and with Billy Lee riding, looks the most likely winner.

Was well beaten over C&D last month when returning from five months off but improved to win comfortably over the same trip at Tipperary four weeks ago. Has now won one and placed in five of her eight starts. Sam Coen's 7lb claim will help. Should be involved at the finish.
Unlucky not to win on penultimate start from a mark of 90 and was overfaced in a Listed race last time. Back down into a handicap here and off a mark of 89, looks like something to bet on.

Had been off the track for 6 months when making a satisfactory return here over 5f six weeks ago, finishing a close up 3rd. Shaped as though the run was just needed then but ran no sort of race back here last time when last of 12 over a slightly longer trip, albeit in a tougher race. Moves into handicaps now and can bounce back and feature.
Makes handicap debut and Hayes has been booked. Was green when winning last time on just her 2nd run, but was given a very confident ride and won cosily. Will improve.

Was beaten less than a length when finishing third over 1m 3f at Dundalk last month but was a well beaten fifth when stepped up to 1m 4f here eight days later. Drop back in trip should suit. Should be thereabouts.
Having won previously over hurdles he has shown some ability on the flat without yet making the frame. Runs off a reasonable mark here and should be suited by the drop in distance.

Mastastroque is a 4-year-old gelding trained by J A Stack. He is 0-4 wins and hasn't shown a great deal yet. He heads the weights in this weak-looking 0-60 handicap. Stepped up in trip to 10.5f, which should suit being out of the 121 rated Derby winner Masar. J A Stack also puts on first-time cheekpieces, and J A Stack has 26/75 places and 8/75 wins when putting on first-time cheekpieces, so they seem to bring about some improvement. Andrew Slattery rides, which is always a positive, with 16/65 wins and 37/65 placed if J A Stack's charge is 15-2 or less. Big each-way shout.

Tartaraghan is still a maiden after 21 starts, but she has been placed 6 times. The last of those was at Navan last October off a 3 lbs higher mark. She was well beaten on her return at Leopardstown last week, but that was over 1m4f. She will benefit from the run, and the drop in distance makes her a good EW bet with 5 places on offer.

Nibras Rainbow is a small each-way tip, today's NAP selection , definitely needs to improve on that last run when finishing 5th over 1m4f. Now drops down in distance to 1m2f which may be more suitable, most of his best form has been at a shorter distance. Today is only his 3rd run back from a rest so he could do better yet this year, possibly in better shape fitness wise today. Runs from a 3lb lower mark than last time. Good draw , good jockey in the saddle.

I’m going to take a chance that SLANEY SWAGGER is ready to go on his first run of the season for Philip Byrne. I’m drawn in partly because this small Offaly-based stable landed a touch yesterday in Roscommon with ‘Out on Friday’. Another reason I’m drawn is this lad’s mark is dropping like a stone, down to 59 from a high of 79. He’ll surely have his day. He seems to be ground versatile; he has form on soft/heavy and good/firm ground from last season with Jim Bolger. The first-time blinkers and Martin Hassett's 5lb all draw hope. Looking for double-digit winners carries risks, but I’ll roll the dice.
